Article Title: 'Internet access is fundamental right': SC suggests ‘child mode’ for social media accounts
Article Text:
Blanket restrictions are not the answer

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Saturday declared access to and use of the internet a fundamental right for every individual, including children, under Articles 21 and 19(1)(a) of the Constitution, observing that “The safety of our children and their freedom are not at odds with each other. ”The bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran also suggested that children’s online safety should be strengthened through measures such as a ‘child mode’ for social media accounts, rather than denying them access to the internet altogether, LiveLaw reported.A bench comprising Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran made the observations while issuing directions to strengthen mechanisms for detecting and removing child sexual exploitation and abuse material (CSEAM) from social media platforms and other online services.According to LiveLaw, the bench said: "..we have no hesitation in saying that the right to access and use the internet is a fundamental right of every individual under Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution. Our children, irrespective of their age enjoy the same rights, and to deny the same altogether would be as absurd as saying children below a certain age do not have a conscience worth protecting or a freedom of speech worth expressing.The safety of our children and their freedom are not at odds with each other. Our children are entitled to both."The bench acknowledged that the internet, in its present form, poses safety risks to children. However, it said restricting children's access because online platforms had failed to detect and remove harmful material would amount to mistaking the victim for the problem.The court examined whether children should be completely shielded from the internet and social media in the interest of their safety. It noted that the right to freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a) includes the right to know, receive and impart information and ideas.Describing the internet as a marketplace of ideas, creative expression and information, the court said its value extended beyond the material available online to the opportunities it provided for learning, communication and access to information."For many children, particularly in remote areas, it is often the only source of learning and information," the court observed.It also noted that the internet could be particularly important for children with special needs, for whom online platforms might be the only place to find companionship with others facing similar circumstances.The bench referred to the Supreme Court's 2020 judgment in Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India, which held that "the freedom of speech and expression and the freedom to carry on any trade or business through the medium of the internet is constitutionally protected as a fundamental right under Article 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(g) of the Constitution."In that judgment, the court had refrained from expressing a view on whether the right to access the internet, by itself, constituted a fundamental right.The bench also referred to the 2025 judgment in Pragya Prasun & Ors. v. Union of India, in which the court recognised the right to digital access as a fundamental right under Article 21.
Article Summary: Supreme Court declares access to and use of the internet a fundamental right for every individual, including children. “The safety of our children and their freedom are not at odds with each other. ” bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran said.

Article Title: YouTuber Dhruv Rathee faces court warrants over 2018 video targeting BJP IT cell
Article Text:
Bailable warrants issued against Dhruv Rathee in defamation case linked to 2018 video

NEW DELHI: A Delhi court has issued bailable warrants against YouTuber Dhruv Rathee in a 2018 defamation case, news agency PTI reported.The case stems from a video published by Rathee in May 2018, in which he allegedly claimed that the Bharatiya Janata Party’s ( BJP ) Information Technology cell had attempted to bribe a man to defame him. The video was posted on Rathee’s social media account and later retweeted by Arvind Kejriwal, who was then the Delhi chief minister.The complainant, Vikas Sankrityayan, also known as Vikas Pandey, subsequently initiated defamation proceedings against Rathee and Kejriwal over the video and its circulation.Earlier, on October 12, Judicial Magistrate Rahul Jain of the Saket court ordered fresh summons to Rathee after the complainant submitted that repeated attempts to serve him had remained unsuccessful since the proceedings began.The complainant’s counsel, advocate Samaksh Sharma, told the court that the summons had remained unserved for several years as Rathee primarily lived abroad. The court was informed, however, that Rathee was then in India and residing at an address in Gurugram, Haryana.The magistrate noted that Rathee had first been summoned on July 23, 2019, and that the complainant had continued to pursue service of the summons.The court allowed Pandey to accompany the process server and directed him to deposit the process fee within two days. The next hearing was scheduled for October 17, 2026.Separately, Rathee is facing a defamation suit before the Saket court over a video that allegedly claimed Lord Ram and Goddess Sita consumed meat and alcohol during their exile.The complainants, who identified themselves as Hindu devotees, alleged that the video hurt their religious sentiments. They have also sought an ex-parte ad-interim injunction restraining Google from restoring, hosting, uploading, sharing or disseminating the video, or any video with identical or similar content, after notice and verification of the URL, during the pendency of the suit.
Article Summary: A Delhi court has issued bailable warrants against YouTuber Dhruv Rathee. The case stems from a video published by Rathee in May 2018. The video was posted on Rathee's social media account and later retweeted by Arvind Kejriwal.

Article Title: ‘He spoke to Putin to buy diesel’: Ex-diplomat Fabian after Trump waives sanctions over Russian oil
Article Text:
"President Trump contradicts President Trump... what he says today is not what he might say tomorrow": Ex-diplomat Fabian

Trump pauses sanctions

What it means for India

NEW DELHI: Former diplomat KP Fabian on Saturday questioned the rationale behind the US tariff pressure on India over Russian oil purchases, arguing that Washington’s own decision to waive sanctions-related duties under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act exposed a contradiction in its approach.His remarks came after US President Donald Trump earlier today waived sanctions-related duties under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act.Speaking to ANI, Fabian said, “Trump himself spoke to Putin to buy diesel. If America itself is buying, either it should sanction itself, which is ridiculous."He also argued that the tariff threats against India were a negotiating tactic aimed at securing a favourable trade deal rather than a genuine response to New Delhi’s energy purchases from Russia.“Certain tariffs were imposed, and the court in the United States said that Trump had no business."Fabian said Trump had avoided directly confronting Chinese President Xi Jinping over Russian oil purchases because China was a major buyer of Russian exports and Washington wanted closer engagement with Beijing.“Contrary to the Lindsey Graham Act, President Trump did not dare to mention it to Xi Jinping because China is a top buyer, 50 per cent of Russia’s exports.India comes next at 37 per cent,” he told ANI.However, Trump earlier on Saturday paused provisions of the Graham Act that could have imposed tariffs of up to 100% on goods imported into the US from the five largest buyers of Russian crude oil or natural gas, including India and China.The move comes against the backdrop of rising diesel prices in the US ahead of the November midterm elections and a reported agreement under which Russia would supply diesel fuel to Washington.Trump invoked Section 115 of the Act, which authorises the US president to waive certain sanctions-related provisions and restrictions involving foreign entities.“I have submitted to the Congress a certification that the issuance of such a waiver is in the national interests of the United States and a report explaining the basis for the certification, consistent with section 115(b) of the Graham Act,” Trump said in the order.Russia continues to be the single largest supplier of oil for India. A waiver of tariffs of up to 100% which may have come into place in the coming days means that India can continue importing oil in large numbers from Moscow without any economic fallout.If 100% tariffs had been imposed by the Trump administration, then it would have hit exporters as the US is the largest trading partner for India. At the same time, any sanctions may have rendered Russian crude economically unviable which would have added to the supply crunch at a time when Middle East tensions continue.
Article Summary: Former diplomat KP Fabian questioned the rationale behind the US tariff pressure on India over Russian oil purchases. He argued that Washington’s own decision to waive sanctions-related duties under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act exposed a contradiction in its approach. Fabian said the tariff threats against India were a negotiating tactic aimed at securing a favourable trade deal.

Article Title: ‘Foreign-inspired terrorism no longer visible’: Home Secy Govind Mohan on changing internal security landscape
Article Text:
Home Secy Govind Mohan speaks on changing internal security landscape

NEW DELHI: Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan has said that foreign-inspired terrorism has been largely contained in India, barring a few areas, while homegrown terrorism has nearly been eliminated."Homegrown terrorism has almost ended, while foreign-inspired terrorism is no longer visible in any other part of the country," he said.Speaking in Hyderabad, Mohan also identified narcotics, cybercrime and illegal immigration as key challenges facing Indian Police Service (IPS) trainees."Militant naxalism has come to an end; North East insurgency reduced to minuscule levels," he said.His remarks come amid a push by the Centre for stronger regional cooperation to combat terrorism and organised crime.Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Tuesday called on BIMSTEC member countries to strengthen cooperation against terrorism, disrupt terrorist financing and prevent terrorist networks from establishing safe havens in the region.Addressing the first Home Ministers’ Meeting of BIMSTEC countries in New Delhi, Shah said India follows a policy of “zero tolerance” towards terrorism and stressed the need for collective action to strengthen regional security.“Hosting the first BIMSTEC Home Ministers’ Meeting is a matter of great pride and fortune for India. BIMSTEC, in a way, has become an essential platform for regional integration, economic cooperation and collective security.With the spirit of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, India is going ahead today," Shah said.“We have always been committed to peace, coexistence and human welfare. We continue to be committed to these even today. India has never believed in attacking any country or establishing dominance over them. India has always believed in upholding the sovereignty and territorial integrity of every country and peaceful resolution of differences,” he added.Shah said trust among BIMSTEC members was strengthened by the understanding that each country's security arrangements should contribute to the security of others.He called for a collective commitment to ensure that terrorist networks could not find shelter, establish bases or training facilities, mobilise resources or carry out activities against other member countries.
Article Summary: Militant naxalism has come to an end; North East insurgency reduced to minuscule levels. Home Minister Amit Shah on Tuesday called on BIMSTEC member countries to strengthen cooperation against terrorism, disrupt terrorist financing and prevent terrorist networks from establishing safe havens in the region.

NEW DELHI: Govt defended external affairs minister S Jaishankar's upcoming meeting with US secretary of state Marco Rubio in Mumbai, citing several examples of foreign leaders and ministers being hosted outside of Delhi.The ministry of external affairs also said Jaishankar would be the guest of honour at US's 250th anniversary celebrations in Mumbai.Govt had come under criticism from the opposition for US ambassador Sergio Gor's remark that the Americans expected Jaishankar to join Rubio in Mumbai, with Congress saying the minister had been "summoned".Responding to questions, the ministry said Jaishankar would host not just Rubio on Oct 20 but his UAE counterp-art, Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, in Mumbai a day earlier."It is the practice over the last decade to host foreign dignitaries from time to time in various cities of India. The visit will provide an opportunity to sustain the high-level engagement between the two countries and advance our shared priorities," said Jaiswal.After his "productive" meeting with the UAE minister Thursday, Jaishankar will have another meeting with Al Nahyan Monday. "The delegations will assess and take forward initiatives in the areas of energy, trade and investments, fintech, defence and connectivity," said the official.The ministers discussed West Asia and the Strait of Hormuz situation. "Exchanged perspectives on bilateral and global issues in the spirit of our Comprehensive Strategic Partnership," said Jaishankar in a post on X.
Article Summary: S Jaishankar will host US secretary of state Marco Rubio on Oct 20. Jaishankaar will also host UAE counterp-art Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan a day earlier. The ministers will review bilateral cooperation under India-UAE Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

Article Title: Two vessels carrying 24 Indian seafarers hit by projectiles, drone in separate incidents; all safe
Article Text:
Indian seafarers safe after tanker hit in Strait of Hormuz and another off Romania (representative image)

India has raised concerns over attacks on commercial vessels

India also concerned over attacks in the Black Sea

NEW DELHI: Two vessels carrying a total of 24 Indian seafarers were struck in separate incidents in the Strait of Hormuz and off Romania, Union shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal said on Friday, adding that all crew members were safe and no casualties or injuries had been reported.In a post on X on Friday night, Sonowal said crude oil tanker MT ST 3, carrying 15 Indian seafarers, was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on October 16. In a separate incident on October 14, chemical tanker YARA J, carrying nine Indian seafarers, was hit by a drone at Sulina Anchorage, Romania.“Thankfully, all 24 Indian nationals across both vessels are completely safe with no casualties or injuries,” the minister said.He added that the government was monitoring both situations and remaining in close contact with the ship management companies to ensure the security and well-being of the crew members.The latest incidents come amid repeated attacks on commercial shipping involving Indian seafarers in the Middle East and the Black Sea region.The ministry of external affairs (MEA) had earlier condemned attacks on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz on October 11, describing the recurring incidents as deeply concerning and warning that they risked aggravating an already volatile situation.The ministry said tanker MT PETRO DOLPHIN, carrying 11 Indian seafarers, had reportedly been struck by a drone at Sohar Anchorage. Nine crew members were rescued, while two remained missing.Another vessel, MT VALTHERA, a Marshall Islands-flagged tanker, was struck by an unidentified projectile, causing a fire on board. All 11 Indian seafarers on the vessel were reported safe, the MEA said.The ministry reiterated that the safety and security of Indian seafarers remained a priority for the government and called for immediate de-escalation and a resolution to the conflict between the United States and Iran through dialogue and diplomacy.It also called for an end to attacks on commercial vessels, seafarers and civilian infrastructure, stressing the need to uphold freedom of navigation and the safe, unimpeded movement of maritime commerce through international waterways in accordance with international law.India has also raised concerns over attacks on commercial shipping in the Black Sea. In a separate development the previous week, the MEA condemned further strikes on commercial vessels and called for an immediate cessation of violence in the interest of peace and stability.The ministry had also referred to external affairs minister S Jaishankar’s remarks that India remained in contact with Russia and Ukraine over its proposal for safe shipping in the Black Sea and “non-attack possibilities”, while addressing concerns raised by both sides over grain and energy exports.
Article Summary: Two vessels carrying a total of 24 Indian seafarers were struck in separate incidents in the Strait of Hormuz and off Romania. Union shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal said all crew members were safe and no casualties or injuries had been reported. Latest incidents come amid repeated attacks on commercial shipping involving Indian seafarer in the Middle East and Black Sea region.

Article Title: Ex-IAS Divya Mittal launches own party: 10 civil servants who quit service to enter politics
Article Text:
Mittal launched her party, the Jan Neeti Bharat Party.

1. Yashwant Sinha

2. Ajit Jogi

3. Mani Shankar Aiyar

4. Arvind Kejriwal

5. KJ Alphons

6. Satyapal Singh

7. OP Choudhary

8. Aparajita Sarangi

9. AK Sharma

10. Asim Arun

Bonus: K Annamalai

NEW DELHI: Former IAS officer Divya Mittal on Thursday launched the Jan Neeti Bharat party and announced that it would contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. Her announcement comes nearly a month after she took voluntary retirement from the civil services, ending a 13-year administrative career to pursue politics independently.In a video message on X, Mittal said the party will focus on making people central to policymaking and ensuring that the government remains accountable to them throughout its five-year term, rather than only on election day."Politics rules over you. In Jan Neeti, you will be the ones who rule," she said, announcing the party's name and its decision to contest the state polls due early next year.Her decision to launch a party of her own places her among a group of civil servants who left government service before their scheduled retirement to enter politics.Here are 10 former civil servants who made the transition from bureaucracy to politics before completing their service.Yashwant Sinha resigned from the Indian Administrative Service in 1984 to enter active politics. He joined the Janata Party and subsequently became associated with the Janata Dal before joining the BJP.Sinha first served as Union finance minister in the Chandra Shekhar government in 1990-91.Under Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, he returned to the finance ministry in 1998 and held the portfolio until 2002, when he became external affairs minister.His political career also included membership of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. Sinha later distanced himself from the BJP and joined the Trinamool Congress in 2021, before contesting the 2022 presidential election as the opposition's joint candidate.Ajit Jogi left the IAS in 1986 to enter politics and joined the Congress. He had served as a district collector before moving into political life and was subsequently elected to the Rajya Sabha.Jogi's biggest political breakthrough came in 2000, when Chhattisgarh was carved out of Madhya Pradesh. He became the newly created state's first chief minister, holding office until 2003.After years in the Congress, Jogi broke away from the party in 2016 and founded the Janata Congress Chhattisgarh, seeking to establish an independent regional political platform.His career stands out as an example of a former administrator moving from district-level governance to the leadership of a newly formed state and later attempting to build a party of his own.Mani Shankar Aiyar resigned from the Indian Foreign Service in 1989 to enter politics. He had served as a diplomat for more than two decades and spent part of his career on deputation to the Prime Minister's Office under Rajiv Gandhi.Aiyar joined the Congress and won the Mayiladuthurai Lok Sabha seat in Tamil Nadu in 1991. He went on to become a prominent party leader and served as Union minister for petroleum and natural gas during the UPA government.He also held the panchayati raj portfolio and was involved in efforts to strengthen local self-government institutions.Arvind Kejriwal resigned from the Indian Revenue Service in 2006 after working in the income tax department. He had become involved in the Right to Information movement and founded the non-governmental organisation Parivartan to address citizens' grievances.His political journey gathered momentum during the Ana Hazare-led India Against Corruption movement, which campaigned for a stronger anti-corruption law. In 2012, Kejriwal founded the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), choosing to build a political organisation rather than join an established party.AAP made its electoral debut in the 2013 Delhi assembly elections, when Kejriwal defeated then chief minister Sheila Dikshit. He became Delhi chief minister in December 2013 and returned to the post after the party's victories in 2015 and 2020.KJ Alphons took voluntary retirement from the IAS in 2006 and entered electoral politics in Kerala. He contested the Kanjirappally assembly seat in Kerala as an independent candidate supported by the Left Democratic Front and won.Alphons later founded the Jana Shakti platform before joining the BJP in 2011. His political journey subsequently took him to Parliament, when he became a Rajya Sabha member.In 2017, he was inducted into the Narendra Modi government as Union minister of state for tourism, with independent charge, and also handled electronics and information technology.His transition from a civil servant known for urban development initiatives to a state-level politician and Union minister is an example of an officer moving across political formations during his career.Satyapal Singh, a 1980-batch IPS officer of the Maharashtra cadre, opted for voluntary retirement in January 2014 while serving as Mumbai police commissioner, ahead of the Lok Sabha elections.He joined the BJP and contested the Baghpat Lok Sabha seat in Uttar Pradesh in 2014, defeating Rashtriya Lok Dal chief Ajit Singh. He retained the constituency in the 2019 general election.Singh served as Union minister of state for human resource development and water resources during the Modi government's first term. Before entering politics, he had served in several police leadership roles and was known for his work in law enforcement.OP Choudhary, a 2005-batch IAS officer, resigned from the service in 2018 while serving as Raipur collector to enter politics. He joined the BJP and contested the Kharsia assembly constituency in Chhattisgarh in the same year.Choudhary lost that election but returned to the electoral contest in 2023, this time winning the Raipur City South seat. He was subsequently inducted into the Chhattisgarh government as a minister.His career highlights the uncertain transition from administration to politics. Unlike officers who win their first election, Choudhary's initial defeat did not end his political ambitions. He returned five years later and secured a place in the state Cabinet.Aparajita Sarangi, a 1994-batch IAS officer of the Odisha cadre, took voluntary retirement in 2018 while serving as joint secretary in the Union rural development ministry.She joined the BJP in November that year and contested the 2019 Lok Sabha election from Bhubaneswar. Sarangi won the seat, defeating Biju Janata Dal candidate Arup Patnaik.She retained the constituency in the 2024 general election, establishing herself as a BJP leader in Odisha.Sarangi's transition was particularly swift: she moved from a senior central government position to an electoral contest within months of leaving the service and subsequently secured two consecutive Lok Sabha victories.AK Sharma, a 1988-batch IAS officer of the Gujarat cadre, took voluntary retirement in January 2021, around 18 months before his scheduled superannuation.Sharma had spent a substantial part of his career working in the Prime Minister's Office and was associated with Narendra Modi's administration during his tenure as Gujarat chief minister and later as prime minister.After leaving the service, Sharma joined the BJP and was elected to the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council. He subsequently became a minister in the Yogi Adityanath government, handling portfolios including urban development and energy.His move demonstrated how a senior bureaucrat with experience in the central administration could enter state politics and secure a position in the Cabinet without first contesting a direct assembly election.Asim Arun, a 1994-batch IPS officer, took voluntary retirement in January 2022 while serving as Kanpur police commissioner. He joined the BJP soon afterwards, ahead of the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections.Arun contested the Kannauj assembly seat and won, entering a constituency associated with the Samajwadi Party. He was subsequently inducted into the Yogi Adityanath government.His political entry came within weeks of his voluntary retirement, making him one of the clearest recent examples of a serving police officer moving directly into electoral politics before the end of his career.K Annamalai, a 2011-batch IPS officer of the Karnataka cadre, resigned from the police service in September 2019, before completing his tenure. He had served as superintendent of police in Udupi and Chikkamagaluru districts before leaving the force.He joined the BJP in August 2020 and rose rapidly through the party's ranks. In July 2021, he was appointed the BJP's Tamil Nadu president, becoming one of the party's most prominent faces in the state.Annamalai contested the 2021 Tamil Nadu assembly election from Aravakurichi but lost to the DMK's R Elango. In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, he contested from Coimbatore but lost to DMK candidate Ganapathi P Rajkumar.In June 2026, Annamalai quit the BJP following differences with the party leadership over its political strategy in Tamil Nadu and launched a new political movement, 'We The Leaders'. He said the movement would focus on "common man politics", challenge what he described as "cult and dynastic politics", and eventually evolve into a political party. He has outlined plans to contest the 2031 Tamil Nadu assembly elections.
Article Summary: Divya Mittal launched her party, the Jan Neeti Bharat Party, on Thursday. The party will contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. Her announcement comes nearly a month after she took voluntary retirement from the civil services, ending a 13-year administrative career.

Article Title: India diversified crude oil sources from 27 to 41 amid disruptions in Hormuz, Red Sea: Hardeep Puri
Article Text:
Puri said disruptions to international shipping routes could have a direct impact on Indian industries and household expenses (ANI Photo).

NEW DELHI: India has expanded its crude oil supply network from 27 countries to 41 and will continue to diversify imports, increase refining capacity and explore new sources of oil amid geopolitical tensions, minister for petroleum and natural gas Hardeep Singh Puri said.“We have diversified our sources of supply from 27 to 41,” he said, while speaking at the Pathways to Viksit Bharat Conclave at Shri Ram College of Commerce, ANI reported.Puri said disruptions to international shipping routes could have a direct impact on Indian industries and household expenses.“A disruption along a distant shipping route can alter the costs of an Indian factory and the budget of an Indian household,” Puri said.Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the event, Puri said India was importing more than 5 million barrels of oil per day while exporting around 1 million barrels, supported by its expanding refining capacity.He said India’s crude oil procurement would continue to be guided by the availability of supplies at competitive prices. While governments help establish energy relationships, purchasing decisions are made by commercial entities based on price and availability, he added.Puri cited disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz as an example of the need to diversify energy supplies, given the substantial share of global energy flows passing through the region. He also pointed to emerging tensions in the Red Sea, saying the government was monitoring the situation and working to ensure uninterrupted supplies.The minister said India would also need to raise domestic energy production to meet growing demand as economic expansion and industrial activity drive up consumption.He expressed confidence that the Samudra Manthan scheme, which supports deep-sea oil and gas exploration, would help strengthen domestic output over the next three years. ANI reported.Under the scheme, the government plans to provide resources for drilling 150 wells, Puri said, stressing the need for investment in exploration to unlock the country’s domestic oil and gas potential.
Article Summary: Puri said disruptions to international shipping routes could have a direct impact on Indian industries and household expenses. He said India was importing more than 5 million barrels of oil per day while exporting around 1 million barrels. Puri said India’s crude oil procurement would continue to be guided by the availability of supplies at competitive prices.

Article Title: 'Interfering in electoral practices': India pulls up US lawmaker for claims on voter roll deletions
Article Text:
File photo: US Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal and MEA spokesperson

Indian ambassador also rejects allegations

Election Commission's nationwide revision exercise

NEW DELHI: India on Friday strongly rejected US Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal 's remarks concerning the country's electoral process, calling them “unwarranted and uninformed” and accusing her of interfering in the electoral practices of a fellow democracy.Responding to a question during a bi-weekly media briefing in New Delhi, ministry of external affairs (MEA) spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the remarks undermined democratic principles.“We find the remarks of the Congresswoman unwarranted and uninformed and tantamount to interfering in the electoral practices of a fellow democracy. This is an approach that undermines democracy itself,” Jaiswal said.The response followed Jayapal's expression of concern over reports of names being removed from India's electoral rolls.The Democrat representing Washington state wrote on X, “I am deeply concerned about the actions of the Indian government to purge 130 million people from the voting rolls.”India's Ambassador to the US, Vinay Mohan Kwatra, had also dismissed Jayapal's allegations on Thursday, describing them as interference in India's internal affairs.“The remarks by Rep. Jayapal on India's electoral and political processes are unacceptable interference in India's internal affairs,” Kwatra wrote on X.He added that India had strong constitutional institutions and a long record of conducting free and fair elections.“India is a vibrant democracy with robust, independent constitutional institutions and a longstanding record of free and fair elections. Always open to constructive conversation with the Congresswoman to dispel her misconceptions,” he said.Jayapal, who was born in Chennai, previously served as chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus. She has also clashed with New Delhi in the past, notably moving a resolution in the US House of Representatives in 2019 urging India to lift communication restrictions in Kashmir.Meanwhile, the Election Commission of India (ECI) has been conducting a nationwide Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in multiple phases.The Commission has said lists identifying absent, shifted, deceased and duplicate voters were publicly displayed and shared with political parties.It has also clarified that people whose names have been deleted from the rolls can apply for enrolment at any time.
Article Summary: U.S. Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal expressed concern over reports of names being removed from India's electoral rolls. India's Ambassador to the US, Vinay Mohan Kwatra, had also dismissedJayapal's allegations as interference in India's internal affairs.

Article Title: PM Modi to visit Canada on December 11-12, Mark Carney confirms after phone call
Article Text:
The announcement followed a telephone conversation between PM Modi and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney

India, Canada push to conclude trade deal

Leaders seek to build on improved bilateral ties

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Canada on December 11-12, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said, as New Delhi and Ottawa seek to strengthen bilateral ties and advance cooperation in trade, energy, technology and security.Carney confirmed the dates while speaking to visitors at a restaurant in Calgary on Thursday, saying he had “just spoke” to PM Modi about the upcoming visit. He said the PM Modi would travel to Toronto and Ottawa, adding, “We’ll see if we can broaden it out.”The Indian High Commission in Ottawa subsequently confirmed the December 11-12 visit in a post on X, saying the two leaders had agreed to build on the positive momentum in bilateral relations and work towards concrete outcomes across key sectors.The confirmation came amid renewed diplomatic engagement between the two countries, with both sides pushing to expand economic cooperation and conclude negotiations on a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA).However, the ministry of external affairs had said on Friday that the dates were still under discussion.MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said: “As you are aware, foreign minister of Canada visited India a few days back.She met with the external affairs minister (S Jaishankar) and discussed progress in bilateral ties. She also called on the Prime Minister. During the visit, the PM Modi's visit to Canada came up for discussion. The dates for the visit are presently under discussion. We will announce the visit at the appropriate time. ”PM Modi's proposed visit comes as the two countries seek to conclude negotiations on CEPA by the end of 2026, with the agreement expected to support efforts to double bilateral trade by 2030.Canadian foreign minister Anita Anand discussed the trade pact and ways to expand cooperation during her meeting with Modi in New Delhi earlier this week. The discussions covered trade, investment, energy, education, culture, technology and security.According to a readout issued by the Canadian government, the two leaders also discussed the Team Canada Trade Mission to India, led by Canadian International Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu, as an effort to expand bilateral trade and strengthen Canada's engagement in the Indo-Pacific.“Minister Anand and PM Modi discussed the importance of concluding a comprehensive economic partnership agreement by the end of the year and highlighted the Team Canada Trade Mission led by International Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu as a tangible example of growing the economic partnership, expansion of bilateral trade and advancing Canada's broader engagements in the Indo-Pacific,” the statement read.Following the meeting, Modi described the discussions as productive and reiterated India's commitment to strengthening ties with Canada.“Pleased to meet Canadian foreign minister Anita Anand. We had a productive discussion on further strengthening India-Canada ties in trade, technology, security, energy, education and people-to-people exchanges,” PM Modi said in a post on X.“India is committed to building a constructive and forward-looking strategic partnership with Canada that delivers tangible benefits to the people of both countries,” he added.Anand also expressed optimism about the relationship, saying the two countries had considerable scope to expand cooperation in trade, investment and security.“Canada and India have enormous potential to shape a more prosperous future, together. I had the opportunity to meet with Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi today to discuss our strategic partnership and the opportunities ahead for trade, investment and security,” she said.“From Prime Minister Carney's visit earlier this year to the Team Canada Trade Mission underway, our renewed engagement reflects a growing ambition to turn shared priorities into lasting opportunities for both nations,” Anand said, adding that Canada looked forward to welcoming PM Modi in December.The planned visit follows a telephone conversation between PM Modi and Carney earlier this week, during which the two leaders discussed strengthening the India-Canada strategic partnership.PM Modi described the conversation as warm and productive, stressing the importance of closer cooperation between the two countries.“Together, India and Canada are contributing towards a more stable and prosperous world,” PM Modi said in a post on X.According to the Canadian Prime Minister's Office, the two leaders reaffirmed their commitment to concluding CEPA negotiations at the earliest opportunity and advancing efforts to double bilateral trade by 2030.Anand's visit also included discussions on the progress made under the India-Canada joint roadmap. The two sides welcomed a bilateral security dialogue held in India the previous week as part of continued engagement on security and law enforcement at the national security adviser level.The renewed diplomatic engagement comes as India and Canada seek to translate improved political ties into tangible cooperation across economic and strategic sectors.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi will visit Canada on December 11-12, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said. Announcement comes amid renewed diplomatic engagement between the two countries. Article Title: Higher duties at lower pay amount to workplace exploitation, says J&K HC

JAMMU: Compelling an employee to discharge the responsibilities of a higher post while paying him a lower salary amounts to workplace exploitation, which is impermissible in law, Jammu & Kashmir high court ruled.A division bench comprising Chief Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati and Justice Rajesh Sekhri made the observations while dismissing J&K govt’s appeal against a single bench order granting substantive promotion and consequential benefits to a municipal employee.The petitioner, Ghulam Mohammad Sheikh, was engaged as a daily wager in Sopore municipal council in 1980, and his services were regularised in 1988.In his petition, Sheikh said while his similarly situated colleague, Khazir Mohammad Shah, was promoted as jamadar/sanitary supervisor in 1994, he was denied the promotion despite having been regularised in the same year.He subsequently approached the high court, which in 1999 directed the authorities to consider his claim for promotion. However, the direction was not implemented in letter and spirit.Allowing Sheikh’s petition on May 2, 2023, the single bench held that he should be deemed substantively appointed and promoted as sanitary supervisor from April 28, 2005, with all consequential benefits.Sheikh had been performing the duties of jamadar/sanitary supervisor since June 2000, initially in his own pay and grade and subsequently with charge allowance from April 28, 2005.The UT administration challenged the verdict before the division bench, contending that merely performing the duties of a higher post did not confer any right to substantive promotion or the corresponding pay scale.Rejecting the govt’s contentions, the bench said although an employee ordinarily cannot claim the pay scale of a higher post merely because he has performed its duties, an exception exists where the employee has been formally ordered to discharge the responsibilities of that post.The division bench found no illegality or impropriety in the single bench order and upheld its directions.
Article Summary: J&K govt dismissed appeal against a single bench order granting substantive promotion and consequential benefits to a municipal employee. The petitioner, Ghulam Mohammad Sheikh, was engaged as a daily wager in Sopore municipal council in 1980, and his services were regularised in 1988. The division bench found no illegality or impropriety and upheld its directions.

NEW DELHI: The home ministry Friday expanded the pool of enumerators for the Census exercise, making teachers of not just govt schools but also that of aided or unaided private bodies, societies and trusts; and clerks or officials employed not just by central and state govts but also by public sector undertakings, banks etc, eligible for the assignment.Amending Census Rules 1990, the ministry, in a notification issued Friday, expanded the description of staff who can be hired as enumerators for Census 2027, the second phase of which is due to start in five poll-bound states in Nov, followed by the remaining states (barring the snow-bound UT of Ladakh and parts of Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh and J&K where it is already over) in Feb next year.The description of those who can be hired as enumerators — encapsulated in Rule 3 of the Census Rules — has been revised from “teachers, clerks or any official or any person” to three distinct categories.Among teachers, those employed in any educational institution of govt, local authority, aided or unaided private bodies, societies or trusts will be eligible to be hired as enumerators. NEW DELHI: As climate change alters ocean temperature, marine habitats and distribution of fish stocks, scientists from govt institutions, including Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), have called for using satellite-based decision support systems and a framework for sustainable fisheries management in the country where the livelihood of about 30 million fisherfolk is linked to fisheries and allied activities.They, while participating in the 47th Asian Conference on Remote Sensing this week, proposed strengthening early warning and fisheries advisories using satellite technologies, underlining that timely information on ocean conditions, potential fishing zones and weather-related risks could help fishers make better-informed decisions.With the climate change leading to marine heatwaves and shifts in the distribution of marine species, affecting fish availability, fishing operations and the livelihoods of communities dependent on marine resources, Shubhadeep Ghosh, ICAR’s assistant director general, said, “These challenges underscore the need for science-based monitoring systems and adaptive fisheries management.”Marine experts, including scientists from ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI) and Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS), during the conference explored the potential of remote sensing to help address these challenges by integrating satellite-derived information on sea surface temperature, ocean colour and other oceanographic conditions with fisheries data, field observations and scientific assessments.They said such integration can strengthen understanding of changing marine environments and support more informed fisheries planning, and pitched for improved communication and last-mile delivery of advisories to translate scientific information into practical benefits.ICAR-CMFRI in its handbook on “application of GIS as a decision support tool in marine fisheries” noted that Remote Sensing (RS) is the first satellite-based technology which overhauled marine fisheries prediction, based on ocean temperature, ocean colour and chlorophyll content.It said, “Satellite based technologies, which are capable of handling spatial data, revolutionized natural resource management over a period of time".

NEW DELHI: The Centre has approved investments worth Rs 1,194.92 crore to upgrade five clusters of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) across Maharashtra, Odisha and Jammu & Kashmir, taking the cumulative investment cleared under the PM-SETU scheme to Rs 3,687 crore.The five projects will be implemented in partnership with Tata Steel Foundation, BVG India, Belrise Industries, Eagle Infra India and Inderdeep Infra India. She also urged the clusters to work towards ISO certification and include at least one WorldSkills-aligned trade or competency area in their approved implementation plans.She said progress in Jammu & Kashmir was encouraging and reflected a commitment to strengthening skilling and expanding opportunities for young people in the region.Under the approved plans, state governments, industry partners and participating ITIs will work together to upgrade facilities, introduce new-age training programmes and improve the relevance of courses to employers’ requirements.The steering committee also reviewed progress under the scheme’s Training of Trainers component. Article Title: Valid ID cards, 'impartial' reporting, basic first-aid: Press Council issues guidelines for journalists covering anti-SIR protests
Article Text:

(With ANI inputs)

NEW DELHI: The Press Council of India (PCI) has issued guidelines for journalists covering the ongoing protests in Delhi against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, saying the measures are aimed at "ensuring the safety of media personnel while enabling them to carry out their professional duties effectively. "According to a PCI release, the council adopted the "Guidelines for Journalists Covering Protests and Demonstrations" at a meeting on Thursday.The guidelines advise journalists to carry valid identity cards issued by their organisations or accreditation from the Press Information Bureau (PIB) or the Directorate of Information and Publicity (DIP), and keep them visibly displayed. They should calmly identify themselves to law enforcement personnel, maintain neutrality, avoid provoking confrontations and follow lawful instructions, particularly those issued for safety reasons.On safety, the PCI urged journalists to maintain a reasonable distance from confrontations, move cautiously through crowds and continually reassess their surroundings. It also cautioned against attaching cameras or recording equipment to police barricades, vehicles or other equipment in ways that obstruct movement or damage property.“Move carefully through crowds, taking short steps to reduce the risk of falling or being trampled.Continuously reassess your position in relation to protesters, counter-protesters, police, and other potential sources of danger,” the guidelines said.Journalists should remain alert to changes in crowd behaviour, approaching individuals, potential confrontations, shifts in crowd noise and emerging hazards. They should also identify and regularly reassess escape routes, including nearby exits, open streets, sidewalks and safe locations. In the event of smoke or tear gas, they should use visible landmarks and safe routes to leave the affected area without moving further into the crowd.The PCI also advised journalists to carry a compact safety kit containing first-aid supplies, water, snacks, a flashlight, a washcloth and eye protection. Depending on the assessed threat, they should consider wearing protective headgear and body armour. Journalists should learn basic first aid and avoid touching tear-gas canisters, flash-bang devices or smoke grenades.On coordination, the guidelines call on newsrooms to designate a point of contact to track journalists’ locations and respond to emergencies. Freelancers, meanwhile, should ensure that a trusted editor or contact knows their location, assignment plan and expected return time.For planned demonstrations, media organisations should coordinate with police and public information officers to clarify communication protocols and identify designated media staging areas.Emphasising journalistic ethics, the Council called for accurate and impartial reporting, urging journalists to distinguish verified facts from allegations and unconfirmed claims and to verify information through multiple sources. Statements from protesters, organisers, police and government authorities should be subjected to equal journalistic scrutiny, with claims clearly attributed.The guidelines also caution against publishing real-time police positions or escape routes if doing so could compromise safety. Journalists should describe observable actions rather than speculate about motives and exercise particular care when filming minors, injured people and private citizens in distress.The council stressed that equipment, live-broadcast commitments and pressure to obtain exclusive footage should never take precedence over journalists’ safety.
Article Summary: The Press Council of India has issued guidelines for journalists covering the ongoing protests in Delhi. The measures are aimed at "ensuring the safety of media personnel while enabling them to carry out their professional duties effectively" The guidelines advise journalists to carry valid identity cards issued by their organisations.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your top concern regarding pollution in Delhi? Landfill waste Air quality Water quality (Yamuna) Dust pollution 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Focus on pollution and waste management

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: Trillion dollar gap: US budget deficit swells to nearly $2 tn in fiscal 2026
Article Text:
US annual budget gap touches $2 trillion

Interest burden grows alongside US debt

Supreme Court ruling leads to $145 billion in tariff refunds

The US government spent nearly $2 trillion more than it collected in the 2026 fiscal year, widening its budget deficit to the higest in five years. Higher debt payments, tariff refunds and increased spending on social benefits and defence contributed to the rise.The shortfall increased by $217 billion from the previous year, reaching $1.99 trillion, according to figures released by the treasury department on Friday.The deficit, recorded in the year to September 30, was the largest in five years and the third-largest annual shortfall on record. It was also the first full fiscal year of President Donald Trump's second term. The last time the US recorded a bigger deficit was in fiscal 2021, when the shortfall reached $2.77 trillion amid spending on Covid-19 pandemic relief measures.The latest figures show that although government revenue rose to a record, expenditure grew considerably faster. Receipts increased by $169 billion, or 3%, to $5.40 trillion in fiscal 2026 from $5.24 trillion a year earlier. Outlays, meanwhile, rose by $386 billion, or 6%, to an unprecedented $7.40 trillion, compared with $7.01 trillion in fiscal 2025.The resulting gap was wider than the $1.78 trillion deficit recorded in the previous fiscal year.The cost of servicing the government's debt continued to weigh on public finances, with debt-service expenditure reaching a record $1.36 trillion. The amount was $144 billion, or 12%, higher than in the previous fiscal year.Debt servicing is now the government's third-largest spending category, surpassed only by Social Security and the combined expenditure on Medicare and Medicaid. The increase comes after total US debt crossed $40 trillion about two months ago.Rising expenditure on social benefit programmes, including Social Security and Medicare, also contributed to the higher deficit. Defence spending recorded another substantial increase, rising by 6% to $917 billion during the fiscal year, up $48 billion.A treasury official told Reuters that the department could not determine how much of the increase in defence expenditure was linked to the war Trump and Israel started against Iran earlier this year.The government's tariff collections took a hit after a Supreme Court ruling this year invalidated a large portion of the tariffs imposed by Trump during his first year in office.The ruling led to $145 billion in tariff refunds during fiscal 2026. Net tariff receipts consequently fell by $22 billion, with net tariff income declining 11% to approximately $173 billion. The reduction in collections was another factor behind the widening budget gap.The treasury department estimated the deficit at 6.2% of GDP for fiscal 2026. This was higher than the actual deficit-to-GDP ratio of 5.8% recorded in fiscal 2025. A Treasury official, however, declined to specify the GDP estimate used to calculate the latest ratio.The final month of the fiscal year also ended in deficit. The US government recorded a $27 billion shortfall in September, compared with a surplus of $198 billion in the same month a year earlier.
Article Summary: The shortfall increased by $217 billion from the previous year, reaching $1.99 trillion. The last time the US recorded a bigger deficit was in fiscal 2021, when the shortfall reached $2.77 trillion amid spending on Covid-19 pandemic relief measures.
